title_candidates: Gemini 4 Argon gets a reusable plan stress test
Try Gemini 4 Argon with a decision pre-mortem
summary: Gemini 4 Argon is reaching paid Gemini accounts. A fictional-plan exercise tests its instruction following through one reusable, reversible Skill.

primary_source.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
primary_source.author: Koray Kavukcuoglu
key_facts: Google began a global Gemini 4 Argon rollout on October 13, 2026.
Consumer access is limited to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search; the announcement does not list free-plan access.
Developers can use Argon through the paid Gemini API tier in AI Studio and Android Studio, while enterprises can use the API, Gemini for business, and Antigravity.
Google lists an introductory API price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising after November 30, 2026.
Google presents Argon as a deep-reasoning model for complex work and reports benchmark and internal deployment gains; these are vendor claims rather than independent guarantees.
The Gemini app lets eligible users select Argon manually and choose Low, Medium, or High thinking, subject to plan and usage limits.

supporting_sources.title: About Gemini models
key_facts: Google's help page lists Argon for personal Google AI Pro and Ultra accounts in Chat and Task modes.
Users can select a model from the prompt box and optionally choose Low, Medium, or High thinking.

supporting_sources.title: Create and manage skills for Gemini Apps
key_facts: Skills save reusable instructions for Gemini chats and tasks and are gradually rolling out to personal accounts.
Creating a Skill requires age 18 or older, a personal Google Account, and Keep Activity turned on.
Skills can be invoked with a slash or at-sign shortcut and can be deactivated from Customize > Skills.

prerequisites: A personal Google Account for someone age 18 or older
An active Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription
Gemini 4 Argon and Skills visible after rollout
Only the fictional, non-sensitive plans below

steps.instruction: Open gemini.google.com, sign in, click the current model name in the prompt box, and select Gemini 4 Argon. Stop rather than substitute another model if Argon is absent.

Choose Customize in the sidebar (open More first if needed), then Skills > Create > Create manually. Name it decision-premortem. Tell it to restate the goal and constraints; list exactly five failure modes; score likelihood and impact from 1–5; propose one cheap, reversible test per failure; list assumptions; finish with one stop condition; never take external actions; and ask one question if a key constraint is missing. Click Create.

Start a new Argon chat, type / (or @ if shown), select decision-premortem, and submit: 'Fictional plan: I have $100 and one Saturday to run a ten-person neighborhood swap in a free community room. No participant data, payments, or bookings are involved. Stress-test this plan.' Check for five failure modes, numeric ratings, reversible tests, assumptions, and a stop condition without any external action.

Invoke the Skill again with: 'Fictional plan: use three evenings and free household materials to build a tabletop marble run for a family game night.' Confirm that Argon keeps the same structure while adapting the analysis; ask it to repair any omitted field.
Reverse the setup through Customize > Skills > decision-premortem > More > Deactivate.

risk_flags: Argon requires Google AI Pro or Ultra and may not have reached every account yet.
Skills are gradually rolling out, require a personal account and Keep Activity, and are unavailable in Temporary chat.
The guide uses fictional inputs because Keep Activity stores prompts; users should not add personal, confidential, legal, medical, or financial information.
Gemini output can be inaccurate and should not be treated as professional advice.
Google benchmark and deployment figures are vendor-reported and were not independently reproduced.
